ckad.title: CKAD independent rehearsal

tasks.title: Build the workload
tasks.task: Create a two-replica information service with explicit image, labels, requests/limits and readiness. Use an original page marker and a ConfigMap. Choose an appropriate controller.
tasks.evidence: Saved manifests; two Ready replicas; correct page from the workload.
tasks.solution: Use a Deployment whose selector matches its template. Mount the page ConfigMap. Validate rollout and response separately.

tasks.title: Deploy and recover
tasks.task: Render a Kustomize overlay or Helm package, change a version, introduce a bad image and restore the known-good revision.
tasks.evidence: Rendered YAML; stalled-rollout evidence; successful recovery and response.
tasks.solution: Inspect rendered names and labels. Read Events for pull failure. Restore the intended Pod template, then check rollout and HTTP. Explain what image rollback cannot undo.

tasks.title: Observe and diagnose
tasks.task: Repair a wrong readiness path and collect current/previous logs where applicable. Explain the resulting traffic effect.
tasks.evidence: Root cause, changed field, readiness and endpoint observations.
tasks.solution: A failing readiness check can leave the process running while removing it from normal Service traffic. Correct the endpoint and repeat the request.

tasks.title: Configure and restrict
tasks.task: Run a non-root compatible worker with a writable scratch volume. Mount a dummy Secret without logging it. Give a separate ServiceAccount Pod-read permissions but no Secret-read permission.
tasks.evidence: Observed UID and allowed write; byte-count-only Secret check; auth can-i yes/no pair.
tasks.solution: Use compatible paths, drop capabilities and disable privilege escalation. Define narrow Role and RoleBinding. Test actual effective permissions.

tasks.title: Connect and explain policy
tasks.task: Expose the workload with a Service and repair a wrong selector. Write an Ingress for the lab host and a NetworkPolicy permitting a labelled frontend. Test routing/policy only where controllers and an enforcing CNI exist.
tasks.evidence: Service request succeeds; backend addresses match; Ingress/controller evidence and allowed/denied policy tests, or explicit not-tested dependencies.
tasks.solution: Service selectors, ports and ready endpoints must align. Ingress needs a controller. NetworkPolicy needs enforcement. Missing infrastructure means the corresponding practical outcome is not earned, even when YAML validates.

ckad.rubric: Award each task’s points only when its stated observable outcomes are demonstrated. Partial credit: split the listed outcomes evenly and document which were observed. 80/100 is this guide’s suggested readiness target, not an official passing score. Repeat all missed tasks independently. If policy or ingress infrastructure is absent, record the attempt as incomplete rather than silently reallocating those points.

cka.title: CKA operations and incident rehearsal

tasks.title: Plan and verify the cluster
tasks.task: In the disposable VM lab, explain the kubeadm/runtime/CNI configuration, RBAC boundaries and control-plane failure model. Demonstrate a supported lifecycle or isolated restore exercise.
tasks.evidence: Version inventory, access checks, sanitized runbook and observed recovery verification.
tasks.solution: Match documentation to the actual version. Protect datastore and application backups separately. Verify API readiness and workload behaviour after recovery.

tasks.title: Schedule and maintain workloads
tasks.task: Apply deliberate placement rules, inspect an unschedulable workload and conduct a controlled worker drain with a PDB. Explain metrics prerequisites for autoscaling.
tasks.evidence: Scheduler Events, placement table, allowedDisruptions and request observations.
tasks.solution: Tolerations permit but do not attract. Required placement can leave Pods Pending. Restore healthy capacity before bypassing a budget.

tasks.title: Repair network paths
tasks.task: Diagnose a Service-selector fault, compare DNS and direct-backend tests, and verify an HTTPRoute on a Gateway-capable cluster. Demonstrate an enforced NetworkPolicy allow/deny pair.
tasks.evidence: EndpointSlices, DNS outcomes, route conditions and both allowed/denied traffic.
tasks.solution: Separate naming, selection, policy and forwarding. CRDs or accepted manifests alone do not prove a controller or policy implementation works.

tasks.title: Explain and recover storage
tasks.task: Inspect binding mode, topology, access mode and reclaim policy. Demonstrate data persistence after Pod replacement and explain a separate restore plan.
tasks.evidence: PVC/PV/class details, new Pod UID, preserved marker and backup scope.
tasks.solution: Persistence is not backup. Reclaim policy can destroy backing storage; inspect it before cleanup.

tasks.title: Diagnose controlled incidents
tasks.task: Resolve a stopped kubelet in the VM lab, a bad workload image and an unavailable application route. Collect evidence before each repair.
tasks.evidence: Symptom, hypothesis, decisive observation, minimal repair and repeated acceptance test for each fault.
tasks.solution: Use host tools when the node/API path is broken. Read image pull Events for registry failures; inspect endpoints and ports for application routing. A reboot alone does not explain cause.

cka.rubric: Original 120-minute training exercise, not official exam questions or scoring. Award points only for demonstrated outcomes; divide task points across its stated outcomes for partial credit. Suggested readiness target: 80/100 plus successful repetition of missed tasks. Infrastructure-dependent tasks remain incomplete when their required lab is unavailable.

ace.title: ACE · Operate a cloud learning environment
ace.rubric: Original practice, not the official exam format. Score evidence out of 100: award each task proportionally for correct configuration, observed verification and explanation. 80 is a suggested internal practice target, not a certification pass mark. Any wrong-project change, exposed credential or unverified cleanup requires correction before claiming readiness. Offline designs are valuable but do not earn live-execution evidence.

tasks.title: Establish scope and spending controls
tasks.task: Identify your sandbox principal, project, region, enabled APIs and billing linkage. Document a budget notification and a complete cleanup inventory before creating resources.
tasks.evidence: Sanitised read-only output, budget recipient and resource inventory with owner/location.
tasks.solution: Distinguish the CLI account, active configuration and explicit project flags. A budget notification is not a cap. Include retained disks, addresses, logs and backups in inventory.

tasks.title: Run and verify the information page
tasks.task: In an authorised sandbox, deploy bank.yaml to a learning GKE cluster with a dedicated kubeconfig. Keep access through port-forward. Explain any changed Pod requests.
tasks.evidence: Context, cluster location, Ready state, usable endpoints and actual Harbour Bank response; clearly label any infrastructure prerequisites already supplied.
tasks.solution: Cloud provisioning, client connectivity and Kubernetes authorization are separate. Confirm scope, wait for rollout, inspect endpoints and test the response. Do not count a dry-run as runtime success.

tasks.title: Bound report access
tasks.task: Use Workload Identity Federation for a dedicated KSA to read one dummy bucket. Prove that an ungranted write is denied.
tasks.evidence: Identity mapping and policy scope, allowed dummy read, denied write, no credential payloads.
tasks.solution: Use the exact project number, workload pool, namespace and KSA. Direct principal binding or documented impersonation must match the selected method. Do not solve access failure with broad Owner grants.

tasks.title: Diagnose one controlled service fault
tasks.task: Introduce a wrong selector on the disposable bank Service. Diagnose and restore it using the smallest justified change. Connect cloud and cluster observations where relevant.
tasks.evidence: Before/after selector, EndpointSlice state, hypothesis and the same request repeated after repair.
tasks.solution: Ready Pods alone cannot establish Service health. Compare selection and labels before altering the Deployment. Restore the known manifest and verify the original request.

tasks.title: Handover and cleanup
tasks.task: Write an operational note and remove only created lab resources after collecting evidence. Explain the remaining billable dependencies or retention obligations.
tasks.evidence: Inventory reconciled against actual resources, cleanup outputs and an honest list of untested operations.
tasks.solution: Cluster deletion alone may not remove every disk, backup, address or stored image. Review each created resource, its retention and owner. Do not delete a shared project as a shortcut.

pca.title: PCA · Defend the Harbour Bank architecture
pca.rubric: Original scenario workshop and reasoning questions, not official exam questions or a replica of Google’s exam format. Score out of 100 for requirements, coherent decisions, failure analysis, evidence and clear communication. A suggested internal review target is 80, with no unresolved critical access or recovery contradiction. Illustrative business targets below are fictional teaching constraints, not industry or regulatory requirements.

tasks.title: Requirements and platform choice
tasks.task: A fictional team of six supports the information page and plans a report service. Traffic peaks at ten times baseline; the team has limited Kubernetes operations experience. Compare Cloud Run, GKE and a VM fleet, then choose with stated assumptions.
tasks.evidence: A decision record, rejected alternative, owner matrix and a trigger for revisiting the choice.
tasks.solution: A simpler managed platform may fit the current application. GKE needs a requirement that justifies its operating model. Separate today’s read-only page from a proposed transactional platform; do not claim an implementation you have not built.

tasks.title: Identity and data boundaries
tasks.task: Reports must remain private; release automation must not read their contents. Draw workload, deployment and human access paths. Design a future transfer service’s retry/idempotency boundary without implementing real payments.
tasks.evidence: Trust-boundary diagram, scoped roles, denial tests and a transaction/idempotency explanation.
tasks.solution: Separate deployer and runtime identities; protect delegation. Use durable storage semantics for business effects. A Kubernetes restart or queue delivery feature does not make two financial writes atomic.

tasks.title: Recovery and migration
tasks.task: For fictional planning, assume a 60-minute RTO and 15-minute RPO for the report service. Design recovery after region loss and migration from an existing environment. Challenge whether the targets are achieved or merely proposed.
tasks.evidence: Dependency inventory, restore order, data checkpoint, quota/key assumptions, cutover and post-write rollback plan.
tasks.solution: Include configuration, images, data, identity and network. Backup for GKE is not a complete project backup. Measure recovery in rehearsal; account for replication lag and write reconciliation after cutover.

tasks.title: Operations and cost
tasks.task: Define a request-based SLO, an actionable alert, an upgrade process and a cost estimate with assumptions. Explain what changes if traffic grows tenfold for a week.
tasks.evidence: Numerator/denominator/window, runbook owner, maintenance checks, capacity constraints and a dated cost model.
tasks.solution: Avoid equating request success with fixed downtime minutes. Include telemetry, storage, transfer and load balancing in costs. Quota, address space and downstream capacity can block autoscaling.

tasks.title: AI help assistant design review
tasks.task: Add a public-help assistant without account access. Explain retrieval, evaluation, prompt-injection handling and fallback. Include one reason to reject a more complex model platform.
tasks.evidence: Data-flow diagram, authorised corpus, hostile/unanswerable test cases, quality/latency criteria and escalation behaviour.
tasks.solution: Retrieved passages are untrusted data, not authority. Restrict sources before generation, test grounding and leakage, and keep financial actions outside the model’s permissions. Managed APIs may reduce operational burden when their data and capability constraints fit.
